title: A Phone Call About a Suspicious Text Message
script: Dimas: [warmly] Ayu, I just got a strange text saying my bank account is blocked, and I need to click a link right now to fix it.
Ayu: Wait, don't click anything yet. Can you read me exactly what the message says, word for word?
Dimas: [thoughtful] It says my account will close in two hours unless I confirm my details immediately through this link.
Ayu: That sounds urgent on purpose, which is exactly how these scam messages usually work. Real banks rarely threaten you like that.
Dimas: [carefully] But what if it's actually real? I don't want to lose access to my money because I ignored it.
Ayu: I understand the fear, although panicking is exactly what these messages are designed to make you feel.
Dimas: [reflective] So what should I do instead of clicking the link they sent me?
Ayu: Open your banking app separately, or call the number printed on your actual bank card, not any number from that text.
Dimas: [honestly] Okay, give me a moment. I'm opening the app now to check if anything seems wrong.
Ayu: Take your time. I'll stay on the phone with you until you're sure everything is fine.
Dimas: [gently] My account looks completely normal here, no blocks, no warnings, nothing unusual at all.
Ayu: The message is highly suspicious, but the app alone does not prove every fact. Contact the bank through its official channel if you need confirmation.
Dimas: [encouraging] I almost clicked it without thinking, because the message genuinely scared me for a second.
Ayu: That's exactly why these messages work on so many people, even careful ones like you sometimes.
Dimas: [sincere] What should I do with the message now? Just delete it and forget about it?
Ayu: Report it through your phone, carrier, or the bank’s official guidance, then block and delete it. Do not forward the live link to friends.
Dimas: Thank you for staying calm with me. I probably would have clicked it if I were alone right now.
Ayu: Pause and verify independently. If you already clicked or entered information, contact the bank immediately and secure any exposed accounts and passwords.

quiz.question: What did the suspicious text message claim?
options: His bank account would close unless he confirmed details through a link
He needed to update an app
quiz.explanation: The message claimed his account would close in two hours unless he confirmed his details through a link.

quiz.question: Why does Ayu think the message is a scam?
options: It creates urgency on purpose, and real banks rarely threaten customers like that
It came from an unknown number
quiz.explanation: Ayu says the urgency is created on purpose, and real banks rarely threaten customers that way.

quiz.question: What does Ayu advise Dimas to do instead of clicking the link?
options: Open his banking app separately or call the number on his bank card
Reply to the text asking questions
quiz.explanation: She advises opening the banking app separately or calling the number printed on his actual bank card.

quiz.question: What did Dimas find when he checked his account?
quiz.explanation: His account looked completely normal, with no blocks or warnings.

quiz.question: What does Ayu suggest Dimas do with the scam message afterward?
options: Report it, then block the number and delete it
quiz.explanation: She suggests reporting it first, then blocking the number and deleting it afterward.

quiz.question: What technique creates pressure in the message?
options: A short deadline and threat of account closure

quiz.question: How does Dimas verify safely?
options: Call the number inside the message
Use the official app or number obtained independently
quiz.explanation: An independent channel avoids the attacker’s contact path.

quiz.question: Why does a normal app not prove every detail?
options: The message is highly suspicious, but the bank is the authority on account status

quiz.question: What if Dimas already entered a password?
options: Contact the bank immediately, secure the account, and change exposed credentials through trusted channels

quiz.question: What should happen before deletion?
options: Report the message through the phone, carrier, or bank guidance
Send it to the group chat
quiz.explanation: Reporting may help block similar attempts.
